task.description: Rework iteration 2 of Step 2 for ISS-0421: fix step-02b's rework-1 FAIL -- the reserved_headroom/1 accessor was specified to read state.reserved_headroom, but Letflow.Admission.init/1 (admission.ex:220-231) never stores reserved_headroom in state; it is a bare init/1 argument consumed once to compute global_cap, then discarded. The validator required option (a): add reserved_headroom as a genuinely new state field, captured in init/1 from the same binding already used to compute global_cap, so the accessor provably returns the same value that instance's global_cap was derived from -- including for a start_link/1 opts override (e.g. a test). Option (b) (re-deriving from Application.get_env later) was explicitly rejected by the validator and not chosen here.

result.summary:
Read lib/letflow/admission.ex:205-231 directly (not the design doc's own prior paraphrase) to confirm the exact current init/1 clause and state shape: `%{pool_size: pool_size, reserved_headroom: reserved_headroom}` is destructured, `global_cap = max(pool_size - reserved_headroom, 1)` is computed, and the returned state map holds exactly four keys (global_cap, global_in_use, tenants, refs) -- reserved_headroom itself is discarded after computing global_cap, confirming the validator's finding verbatim.

Fix applied to §3b (the only place the state-shape/accessor spec lives, plus its one summary echo in §7): withdrew rework-1's false claim that state.reserved_headroom already existed and that the accessor needed 'no new state field.' The design now explicitly requires Letflow.Admission.init/1's returned state map to gain a fifth, genuinely new field, `reserved_headroom`, set from the SAME `reserved_headroom` argument binding already in scope in that same init/1 clause -- the identical binding used, in the identical function call, to compute global_cap. This is specified as purely additive to the existing four keys (global_cap, global_in_use, tenants, refs): none of those four keys' types or how any existing handle_call clause reads/writes them changes. The state-shape doc-comment at admission.ex:212-219 is specified to be updated to list five keys (shown as a comment/type shape, not executable code, consistent with this doc's no-implementation-code constraint). The reserved_headroom/1 accessor's handle_call(:reserved_headroom, _from, state) clause now reads this newly-added state.reserved_headroom field (not a phantom one).

Re-verified explicitly, per the validator's routing instructions, that this closes the exact gap found: because reserved_headroom is captured in the same init/1 clause, from the same binding, at the same moment as global_cap, the accessor is guaranteed to return the identical reserved_headroom value THAT running instance's own global_cap was derived from -- whether that instance was started from config defaults or from a start_link/1 opts override (e.g. a test starting a distinct, differently-configured Admission instance under its own name). There is exactly one number per instance, sourced once at init/1, never two independently-maintained figures that could drift -- so the algebraic identity global_cap + max_concurrency = pool_size (§3b/§3c) now holds per-instance, not merely for the default-config case, closing precisely the class of gap the validator identified. Option (b) (Application.get_env re-read) was not chosen, consistent with the validator's instruction.

Sections touched: §3b only (state-shape addition specified before the accessor spec; accessor's handle_call description corrected to read the new field; arithmetic-identity paragraph re-verified/restated to explicitly reference the per-instance guarantee and name what gap it closes) and §7 (the Admission bullet in the code-shape summary updated to describe the new state field alongside the accessor, since Admission.ex's state shape is now genuinely touched, not just its public function surface). Nothing else in §3b was altered beyond these hunks (the earlier a-vs-b decision/rejected-alternative reasoning, the accessor's calling-convention shape, and the Poller-consumption description are unchanged verbatim). No other section (§0, §1, §2, §3a, §3c prose beyond the untouched formula, §4, §5, §6, §8) was edited. Confirmed via `git diff --stat` / hunk headers that all changed lines fall within §3b's line range and §7's Admission bullet.
result.routing: Route to Step 2b CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (re-check) to verify: (1) the new reserved_headroom state field is genuinely additive to admission.ex's actual current four-key state map and is captured in init/1 from the same binding used for global_cap (i.e. this is buildable against the real code, not asserted against a non-existent field); (2) the reserved_headroom/1 accessor's handle_call clause now reads a field that will actually exist; (3) the algebraic-identity safety argument is restated correctly and now holds per-instance, including for a start_link/1 opts-overridden instance; (4) no other section, including the 6 sections already passed in iteration 0 and the parts of §3b/§7 not related to this specific fix, was disturbed.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR for re-check of the reworked §3b/§7 sections only.

gate_history.notes: Admission.global_cap arithmetic (pool_size 10 - reserved_headroom 2 = 8) independently verified correct against admission.ex/api_pipeline.ex/config. Peak-concurrency safety argument in section 3b fails: max_concurrency:2 for maybe_refresh_active_instances/1 is a hardcoded literal that must stay equal to Admission's reserved_headroom for the 8+2=10 proof to hold, but nothing derives or enforces that equality -- a future independent change to reserved_headroom would silently break the pool-exhaustion safety bound. All other checks (fault isolation, AC4, sequential-sweep decision, no literal code, 2 of 3 open questions) passed.

Rework 1's live-accessor fix (Letflow.Admission.reserved_headroom/1) is specified to read `state.reserved_headroom`, but admission.ex's actual init/1 never stores reserved_headroom in state -- it is a bare init/1 argument consumed only to compute global_cap, then discarded; the state map holds only global_cap, global_in_use, tenants, refs. The accessor as specified would crash or require silently inventing behavior. Fixing this needs a real, undocumented state-shape change (adding reserved_headroom as a new field, captured at the same init/1 moment as global_cap) that the design explicitly denies making ('no new state field'). Diff confirmed only sections 0/3b/3c/7/8 changed; all iteration-0-passed sections (1,2,3a,4,5,6) untouched and remain passed. Accessor's calling-convention shape (defaulted server arg, GenServer.call delegate) does correctly mirror try_acquire/2 and release/2.
